# Non-Examinable Content {#sec-non-examinable-content}

This section covers all the non-examinable content in the course notes.

## Part I - Foundations

### Chapter 1 - Probability Theory

- You will not be examined on <span class="xref-no-num">[covariance @def-covariance]</span>.
- You will not be examined on <span class="xref-no-num">[correlation @def-correlation]</span>.
- The material in the section named <span class="xref-no-num">[Non-Examinable material @sec-prob-theory-non-examinable]</span> section is **not examinable**.


### Chapter 2 - What is Statistical Inference?

- You will <span class="xref-no-num">[not be examined @sec-types-of-data]</span> on the following **types of data**:
  - **Multivariate data:** All exam questions involve **univariate data**, where each observation $x_i$ is a *single numerical value*.  
  - **Categorical data:** All exam questions involve **numerical data** only; no problems will require modelling categories, labels, or qualitative outcomes.

- You will <span class="xref-no-num">[not be examined @wrn-nonexaminable-specifying-models]</span> on how to *specify a statistical model* (i.e. choosing an appropriate distribution for the data). All exam questions will **explicitly state** the statistical model whenever it is required.
- You will <span class="xref-no-num">[not be examined @def-model]</span> on the formal definition of a **statistical model**.

### Chapter 3 - Types of Inference

- **Prediction** and predictive distributions are <span class="xref-no-num">[not examinable @wrn-nonexaminable-prediction]</span>.

## Part II - Point Estimation

### Chapter 4 - Frequentist Point Estimation


### Chapter 5 - Likelihood

- You will <span class="xref-no-num">[not be examined @wrn-nonexaminable-dependent-likelihood]</span> on computing likelihood functions for **dependent data**.
- You will <span class="xref-no-num">[not be examined @sec-sufficiency]</span> on the concept of **sufficiency**.
  - It is useful background, but no questions will require you to use or prove results about sufficient statistics.

### Chapter 6 - Bayesian Inference


## Part III - Interval Estimation

### Chapter 7 - Frequentist Interval Estimation

- You will <span class="xref-no-num">[not be examined @wrn-nonexaminable-ci-general-strategy]</span> on the <span class="xref-no-num">[general strategy @sec-general-ci-strategy]</span> for **deriving confidence intervals**.
- You will **not be examined** on the derivations of the confidence intervals for Normally distributed data with either:

  - <span class="xref-no-num">[Known Variance @sec-normal-ci-known-var]</span>
  - <span class="xref-no-num">[Unknown Variance @sec-normal-ci-unknown-var]</span>  
  
  However, understanding these derivations can be helpful for **remembering and applying** the confidence interval formulae.

### Chapter 8 - Bayesian Intervals

- You will **not be examined** on **computing analytic HDIs** for any posterior distribution. The exam will only require you to understand, interpret and apply the <span class="xref-no-num">[definition @def-hdi]</span> of an HDI in context.

## Part IV - Hypothesis Testing

### Chapter 9 - Frequentist Hypothesis Testing

- For the <span class="xref-no-num">[likelihood ratio test @sec-lrt]</span>, you do **not** need to remember the name <span class="xref-no-num">[Wilks' Theorem @thm-wilks]</span>. It is sufficient to only remember that **the likelihood ratio test statistic is asymptotically distributed as $\chi^2_1$.**

### Chapter 10 - Bayesian Hypothesis Testing

- Chapter 10 is **not examinable**.



<script>
document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', () => {
  document.querySelectorAll('.revision-header').forEach(header => {
    const toggle = (e) => {
      // Don't toggle if clicking a link
      if (e.target.closest('a')) return;
      
      const expanded = header.getAttribute('aria-expanded') === 'true';
      header.setAttribute('aria-expanded', !expanded);
      const content = document.getElementById(header.getAttribute('aria-controls'));
      content.hidden = expanded;
    };
    
    header.addEventListener('click', toggle);
    header.addEventListener('keydown', (e) => {
      if (e.key === 'Enter' || e.key === ' ') {
        e.preventDefault();
        toggle(e);
      }
    });
  });
});
</script>
